text: Write the declaration convention Chapter 17 recommends, and one that violates it. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___;                                // only the second can call this
answer: List<String> good = new ArrayList<>()|ArrayList<String> bad = new ArrayList<>()|bad.ensureCapacity(100)
explanation: Verified: `0 0`. `ensureCapacity` exists on `ArrayList` and not on `List`, so declaring the interface makes it unreachable — which is the point rather than a limitation. Chapter 22 gives the full argument: the declared type is what the rest of your code sees, so declaring the interface keeps you free to change the implementation and keeps callers from depending on what you did not promise.
